content.comment_body: I came across this topic because it relates to my issue. My setup allows communication between [product_name] (simulated panel) and a real [product_name], and it's working as intended. However, I'm attempting to simulate the connection between the simulated panel and a simulated [product_name] within [product_name] software. When I activate network simulation in [product_name], it indicates simulation is running at a specific IP. However, connection doesn't work. The simulated panel connects fine to the real [product_name], but switching to the IP provided by [product_name] results in no connection. I've also tried using the local IP (127.0.0.1), but nothing succeeds. Does anyone know how to achieve this?

After many attempts, I'm confident that [product_name] software does not simulate [product_name] outside of its own environment. You can simulate interactions between two [product_name] units and that's it. CURRENT STATUS: It's not possible to connect a panel (simulated or real) to a simulated instance in [product_name].

That's correct. In [product_name] software, you can only simulate your [product_name] program and network communication between two simulated [product_name] units. To monitor how your [product_name] program communicates with an HMI, you need to upload your project to a physical device and use the Online Test mode, which lets you observe the project directly on the real hardware. Regards, [user_name]
True, but it's not feasible to simulate every scenario on an operational machine. In my view, this should be seen as a software flaw. And honestly, I think it's a significant issue.
From my perspective, this isn't a bug. Even with real PLCs, it's not realistic to simulate all situations...

Exactly. With actual PLCs, you can't simulate every possible scenario. That's why testing needs to occur on simulated PLCs. Calling it a bug is justified, since available information suggests everything should work, but that's not the case.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are dissatisfied because a simulated connection between a simulated panel in [product_name] and a simulated [product_name] within [product_name] software isn't supported. While connecting a simulated panel to an actual device works, users expect full simulation capabilities but encounter limitations. The lack of transparency about this restriction has led to frustration and users considering it a major issue or flaw in the simulation tool.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to simulate all types of communication, specifically between a simulated HMI panel and a simulated [product_name] in [product_name] software, to enable thorough offline testing and validation.
